world.title: Man eaten alive after entering Amur tiger enclosure at England’s Yorkshire Wildlife Park; police urge public not to share videos
world.summary: A man died after entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster, England, on October 10. The incident involved an Amur tiger, which attacked him. Authorities evacuated the wildlife park following the event. Police have urged the public not to share videos related to the incident, emphasizing the need for respect and sensitivity regarding the situation.

world.title: Smartphone Explosion Saves 15-Year-Old From Brutal Bear Attack In Russia
world.summary: A 15-year-old boy in Russia's Altai region was attacked by a bear while in a remote area with a friend. His smartphone exploded, startling the bear and saving the boy's life. Despite the explosion, he sustained severe injuries from the mauling and burns from the device. The incident highlights the unpredictable dangers of wildlife encounters.

world.title: World News Today Live Updates: Pakistan imposes Governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid terror threats
world.summary: Pakistan has imposed Governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to concerns over terrorism. This decision follows accusations from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government that the provincial administration did not adequately cooperate in counter-terrorism efforts. The situation escalates amid ongoing military actions by a Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis in Yemen, with international implications being considered.

business.title: Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 Teased: A More Traditional Cruiser Based On The X440
business.summary: Harley-Davidson has teased the Sprint 440, a new entry-level cruiser model. It features a classic cruiser silhouette, a scooped seat, and updated hardware, while maintaining the 440 cc engine. The design aims to appeal to traditional cruiser enthusiasts, showcasing Harley-Davidson's commitment to blending modern performance with classic aesthetics in its motorcycle lineup. Further details are expected soon.

business.title: Size SUVs For The Price Of A Hyundai Creta » MotorOctane
business.summary: The Hyundai Creta is a popular SUV in India due to its practicality, features, aesthetics, and reasonable pricing. It accommodates four passengers and their luggage while being compact enough for urban environments. The article explores alternatives that offer larger, more capable SUVs at a similar price point, suggesting potential options for consumers seeking greater size and capability.

business.title: Jobless For 2 Years In US, 61-Year-Old IIT Kanpur Alum Considers Returning To India
business.summary: Gautam Dev, a 61-year-old IIT Kanpur alumnus living in Dallas, Texas, is contemplating returning to India after being jobless for nearly two years. He resigned from his software engineering position in September 2024 due to a relocation requirement. The extended job search has depleted his savings, making it difficult for him to cover rent and bills.

technology.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026: Best OLED TV Deals From Samsung, Sony, LG And Haier
technology.summary: Amazon's Great Indian Festival Sale 2026 features significant discounts on premium OLED televisions from brands like Samsung, Sony, LG, and Haier. The sale includes models ranging from 55 to 77 inches, catering to both home entertainment and gaming needs. Shoppers are encouraged to explore five highlighted deals before making a purchase during this festive event.

technology.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026: Top Gaming Phones At Big Discounts, Check Full List
technology.summary: Amazon's Great Indian Festival 2026 features significant discounts on gaming smartphones from various brands, including Samsung, Redmi, Realme, OPPO, Vivo, and Motorola. The sale highlights devices equipped with powerful processors, high-refresh-rate displays, and large batteries, catering to gamers seeking performance and value. Buyers can explore a range of options, from premium to more affordable models during the event.

technology.title: Nikon and Fujifilm's quiet year isn't the disaster you think it is - I believe these two aging cameras are still class-leading in 2026
technology.summary: Nikon and Fujifilm have experienced a quiet year in camera releases, leading to concerns among enthusiasts. However, experts argue that their current models remain competitive and class-leading in 2026. The longevity of camera gear suggests that existing models still meet user needs despite the lack of new features. Enthusiasts may need to adjust expectations regarding innovation and upgrades.

sports.title: Shedge and Gurjapneet give India A consolation win
sports.summary: India A secured a consolation victory against Australia A in their recent match, scoring 275 runs. Shedge contributed significantly with 66 runs, while Arya and Nigam added 49 and 40 runs, respectively. Nigam's all-round performance, which included taking the wicket of Philippe, earned him the Player-of-the-Match award. Dwarshuis and Sutherland were notable bowlers for Australia A.

sports.title: Shedge, Nigam and bowlers set up India A's consolatory win
sports.summary: India A defeated Australia A by 49 runs in the third and final unofficial ODI in Puducherry, preventing a clean sweep for the visitors. India A scored 275 runs, bolstered by a lower-order batting revival. Tight bowling from the home side contributed to the victory, marking a consolation win in the series. Suryansh Shedge played a key role.

sports.title: Mohammed Shami's India Return Gets Backing After Bhuvneshwar Kumar's Recall: "Deserves An Opportunity"
sports.summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been recalled to the Indian squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series in New Zealand, marking his first appearance since the 2022 T20 World Cup. In light of this, out-of-favour pacer Navdeep Saini has expressed support for Mohammed Shami's return to the national team, stating that Shami deserves another opportunity to play.

health.title: What is lymphedema and who is at risk?
health.summary: Lymphedema is a condition that leads to swelling in limbs or other areas, often following cancer treatment. It occurs when lymphatic vessels or nodes are damaged, blocked, or removed, causing fluid to accumulate in tissues. Symptoms include swelling, heaviness, and skin tightness. Early warning signs and preventive measures are crucial for effective management and treatment of the condition.

health.title: Too much TV may be worse for your brain: Study finds smaller brain volumes in frequent viewers
health.summary: A US study published in Alzheimer’s & Dementia indicates that excessive television viewing may negatively impact brain health, showing smaller brain volumes in frequent viewers. MRI scans revealed that these brain changes were more pronounced in men. The research highlights the importance of considering not just prolonged sitting, but also the activities engaged in during that time.

health.title: How much sunlight do you really need for vitamin D? Apollo expert debunks the 15-minute rule
health.summary: Sunlight's role in vitamin D synthesis is complex, influenced by factors such as time of day, latitude, season, skin pigmentation, clothing, air pollution, and UV exposure. Experts caution against the simplistic 15-minute rule for sunlight exposure. Additionally, natural daylight serves as a crucial environmental signal for regulating the circadian clock, impacting overall health beyond just vitamin D levels.

science.title: Mercury’s Greatest Eastern Elongation 2026: What will happen to the night sky on October 12? Check peak time, locations and visibility
science.summary: On October 12, 2026, Mercury will reach its greatest eastern elongation, appearing approximately 25 degrees east of the Sun. This event will be particularly favorable for observers in the Southern Hemisphere, who will have better visibility. However, skywatchers in India may struggle to see the planet due to its position in the sky during this time.

science.title: Researchers developed tattoo inks that can be switched on with ultraviolet light and made to disappear in sunlight; tests found the colours remained switchable in skin for up to 2.2 years, opening pos
science.summary: Researchers have developed tattoo inks that can be activated by ultraviolet light and made to disappear in sunlight. Tests indicate the colors remained switchable in skin for up to 2.2 years. The team aims to introduce more colors and lower production costs as development continues, while also addressing concerns regarding long-term safety, performance, and practical applications of the technology.

entertainment.title: ‘He irritates me, looks like fraud to me’: Cyrus Broacha slams Farah Khan’s cook Dilip, says his humour feels scripted
entertainment.summary: Cyrus Broacha criticized Farah Khan’s cook, Dilip, during a recent discussion, stating that he finds Dilip's humor to be scripted and feels he resembles a fraud. Despite Broacha's remarks, Dilip has gained popularity through Khan's YouTube vlogs, where he showcases his humor and interactions with celebrities. Many viewers appreciate his charm and engaging personality in the videos.

entertainment.title: 15 Years Later, Ektaa Kapoor Announces The Dirty Picture 2
entertainment.summary: Ektaa Kapoor has announced a sequel to The Dirty Picture, fifteen years after the original film's release in December 2011. The first film starred Vidya Balan, Naseeruddin Shah, Emraan Hashmi, and Tusshar Kapoor, depicting the life of actress Silk Smitha. While details about the sequel's characters and plot remain undisclosed, the project is officially in development.

entertainment.title: Ramayana Part 1 To Release Worldwide On November 5, Advance Bookings To Open On Dussehra
entertainment.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's film Ramayana: Part One is set to release worldwide on November 5, 2026. The announcement resolves previous confusion regarding the release date. The film will be available in all premium formats. Advance bookings for the film will open on Dussehra, providing fans an opportunity to secure their tickets ahead of the release.
